newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria creates six new states.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria creates six new states.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha on Tuesday said six new states had been created to make a total of 36, as part of the transition to civilian rule.

"The principle adopted for the creation of states and local governments was to ensure a fair spread and balancing within the geopolitical zones of the country, applying such criteria as population and land mass among others," Abacha said in a speech on the 36th anniversary of Nigeria's independence.
Three states were created in the northern half of the country and three in the south in the next step in Abacha's plan to return Africa's most populous nation to civilian rule by October 1998.
Abacha also said a committee had been set up to develop an economic plan for Nigeria into the next century, to be headed by former head of state Ernest Shonekan.
Nigeria has been under pressure from western countries for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy but insists it will follow its own course to democracy.
The Commonwealth, a grouping of Britain and its former colonies and protectorates, suspended Nigeria last November after the execution of nine minority rights activists.
However, on Sunday the Commonwealth decided not to apply sanctions and to maintain dialogue with the oil-rich state.
On Monday Nigeria's electoral commission announced the registration of five political parties, but government opponents were not among them.
